    Which law applies to me?

    Ownership and title

    4

    Who owns land and how it is registered

    Constitution of Kenya, 2010Land rights and the three land categories

    Why it matters: it tells us which category your parcel is in, and the 99-year limit applies to non-citizens, not to Kenyan citizens living abroad.

    • Art. 40 Everyone may own property, but this right does not protect property found to have been unlawfully acquired (Art. 40(6)).
    • Art. 60 Land must be held and used fairly, efficiently and sustainably: fair access, security of land rights, transparent and cost-effective land administration, conservation, and no gender discrimination.
    • Arts. 61-64 All land is classed as public, community or private. Private land is registered freehold or leasehold land.
    • Art. 65 A non-citizen may hold land on leasehold only, for no more than 99 years. A company counts as a citizen only if it is wholly owned by citizens.
    Official text (Parliament of Kenya) ↗Checked Oct 2026
    Land Registration Act, 2012Title, searches, boundaries and what registration gives

    Why it matters: this is why we check the official search first, then the ground against the register.

    • s.24 Registration as proprietor vests absolute ownership of the land in that person.
    • s.25 That ownership is subject to the leases, charges and other encumbrances shown on the register, and to overriding interests.
    • s.26 A certificate of title is prima facie evidence of ownership. It can be challenged only for proven fraud or misrepresentation the holder was party to, or where the title was acquired illegally, improperly or through corruption.
    • s.28 Overriding interests bind registered land even if not on the register, for example trusts (including customary trusts), rights of way, and certain statutory charges.
    • s.18 and s.19 The cadastral map shows only approximate boundaries unless the register records that they are fixed. A boundary can be fixed by the Registrar after notice to the neighbours, followed by a survey and plan.
    • s.34 Anyone may obtain an official search of the register entries for a parcel on paying the fee.
    • s.93 An interest acquired during marriage for the use of the spouses is deemed matrimonial property.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026
    Land Act, 2012How land is acquired, held and charged

    Why it matters: a sale agreement that is not properly written and witnessed may not be enforceable, and unpaid rent can threaten a lease.

    • s.7 Title can be acquired through adjudication, compulsory acquisition, settlement programmes, long leases out of private land, or other ways an Act allows.
    • s.12 Public land cannot be allocated until it has been planned, surveyed and serviced, and cannot be sold or subdivided until developed as the lease requires.
    • s.38 A contract to dispose of an interest in land must be in writing, signed by all parties, with each signature witnessed.
    • s.28 and s.29 Land rent is a debt owed to government, payable each year in advance. Late payment attracts interest at 2% a month, or another gazetted rate.
    • Compulsory acquisition The State may acquire land only for a public purpose, with prompt and full compensation. Prompt means within a reasonable time and not more than one year after possession.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026
    Community Land Act, 2016Land held by communities

    Why it matters: an individual cannot give good title to community land, so we check who is really entitled to sell.

    • s.2 and s.4 Community land is land declared as such under Art. 63 or converted into it. It vests in the community, not in individuals.
    • s.6 Until registered, unregistered community land is held in trust by the county government for the community and cannot be sold or converted for private purposes.
    • s.16 and s.18 Registering a community as proprietor vests absolute ownership in it. Its certificate of title is prima facie evidence of ownership.
    • s.15 The community assembly is made up of all adult members. A decision to dispose of community land needs the support of at least two-thirds of registered adult members.
    • s.36 An investment agreement over community land needs approval by two-thirds of adult members at an assembly.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026

    Use and permissions

    3

    What you may do with it and who must consent

    Physical and Land Use Planning Act, 2019Development permission, subdivision and change of use

    Why it matters: land can be perfectly titled and still carry a planning breach that falls on the new owner.

    • s.57 No one may develop land in a county without development permission. Developing without it is an offence, with a fine of up to KES 500,000, up to two months in prison, or both, and the county may require the land to be restored.
    • s.58 An applicant who does not own the land must provide the registered owner's written consent.
    • s.59 Plans and documents must be prepared by qualified, registered and licensed professionals.
    • s.61 The county decides within 30 days, granting with conditions or refusing with written reasons. Appeals go to the County Liaison Committee within 14 days.
    • s.72 The county can serve an enforcement notice for development without permission or in breach of conditions. It can require work to stop or buildings to be altered or demolished.
    • Third Schedule Change of user, subdivision and amalgamation are development-control matters. Subdivision of agricultural land also needs Land Control Board consent.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026
    Survey Act (Cap. 299)Who may survey, plans and beacons

    Why it matters: it is why a boundary job must be done by a licensed surveyor and tied to an authenticated plan.

    • s.2 and s.36 Only a government surveyor or a licensed surveyor may carry out surveys for registrable instruments or that affect boundaries.
    • s.22 Surveys for land registration are done under the direction of the Director of Surveys.
    • s.32 Land is not treated as surveyed or resurveyed until its plan is authenticated. Authenticated plans are presumed genuine (s.43).
    • s.24 and s.27 Boundary beacons must be shown on plans. A grantee should check within 60 days that the marks on the plan are in place, and may ask the Director to inquire if they are not.
    • s.28 and s.29 Owners must take reasonable steps to protect survey marks on their land. Removing, damaging or displacing a beacon without authority is an offence.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026
    Land Control Act (Cap. 302)Consent for dealings in agricultural land

    Why it matters: paying a deposit before Board consent can leave a buyer with a void agreement and only a claim to a refund.

    • s.6 A sale, transfer, lease, mortgage, exchange, partition or other dealing in agricultural land in a land control area is void unless the Land Control Board has consented. So is dividing such land into separately titled parcels, with an exception for land under 20 acres in a planning area.
    • s.8 The application for consent must be made within six months of the agreement, by any party. The High Court may extend the time for sufficient reason.
    • s.7 Money paid under a void transaction can be recovered as a debt.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026

    Family and disputes

    2

    Shared property and where disagreements are settled

    Matrimonial Property Act, 2013Family homes and jointly held property

    Why it matters: a seller's spouse can later challenge a sale of the family home made without their consent.

    • s.2 and s.6 The matrimonial home, household goods, and other property jointly owned and acquired during the marriage are matrimonial property. Trust property, including customary trust property, is excluded.
    • s.7 Ownership of matrimonial property follows each spouse's contribution, and contribution includes domestic work, child care and farm work.
    • s.12 Matrimonial property cannot be sold, given, leased or mortgaged without the consent of both spouses. A mortgage or lease of the matrimonial home needs their written, informed consent. A spouse may protect their interest by caution or caveat.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026
    Environment and Land Court frameworkWhere land disputes are decided

    Why it matters: a clear survey and records are the evidence the Court looks to when a dispute arises.

    • ELC Act, s.13 The Environment and Land Court has original and appellate jurisdiction over disputes about land use, title, tenure, boundaries, compulsory acquisition, land administration, and public, private and community land.
    • s.13(5) It can grant injunctions and preservation orders, declarations, damages, compensation, specific performance and restitution.
    • s.20 The Court may refer disputes to mediation, conciliation or traditional dispute resolution, and must stay proceedings where such a step is a condition before suing.
    • Boundaries For registered land, the Land Registration Act expects boundaries to be fixed under s.19 before a boundary dispute is taken to court.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026

    How we handle your data

    1

    What happens to the documents you send us

    Data Protection Act, 2019How we handle your documents and details

    Why it matters: diaspora clients send us IDs and titles, so we only use them for your request and keep them protected.

    • s.25 Personal data must be processed lawfully, fairly and transparently, limited to what is necessary, and kept only as long as needed.
    • s.30, s.2 and s.32 Processing needs a lawful basis, such as consent. Consent must be express, free, specific and informed, and can be withdrawn at any time.
    • s.26 You can ask what we hold, object to processing, and have wrong or misleading data corrected or deleted.
    • s.18 Data controllers and processors must register with the Data Commissioner, where the Commissioner requires it.
    • s.41 Data must be minimised and protected by technical and organisational safeguards.
    • s.48 to s.50 Sending personal data outside Kenya is allowed only with appropriate safeguards or another listed ground.
    Read on Kenya Law ↗Checked Oct 2026

    Plain-language summaries of the Acts, checked in October 2026 against the texts published by Kenya Law. Section numbers can change when Acts are revised. This is general information, not legal advice or a legal opinion; official texts and qualified professionals prevail.

      FAQs

      Frequently asked questions

      Answers across our three services: on the ground, buying from abroad, and buying and selling plots.

      What does Benchmark Land Surveying do, and how are your services organised?

      Our work is organised around three pillars. On the Ground covers boundary surveys, subdivision and mutation, topographic and drone surveys, and title and registry support. Buying from Abroad covers verification before you send money for land in Kenya. Buy & Sell covers reviewed plots, plot requests and checks before you buy or list. Work is led by a licensed land surveyor.

      How long does a boundary survey take?

      Many boundary surveys can be completed on site within a day. Final documentation depends on plot size, terrain, location, whether beacons are in place and the scope of work. We confirm the expected timeline when we agree the scope with you.

      What documents should I have before I start?

      Usually a copy of the title deed or lease, the registered owner's ID, a recent official search, and rates and land rent receipts. A deed plan or registry index map sheet helps for survey work, and a signed sale agreement helps if you are buying. If you are missing something, tell us. We will say what to obtain and from where.

      What is the Virtual Benchmark Land Intelligence Check, and is it a legal opinion?

      It is a guided online screen of your land matter. You answer questions specific to the service you need, and it produces a Benchmark Virtual Report™ showing what to resolve first, what to close and what to confirm. It is based only on the information you provide. It is not legal advice, an official search or a survey. The full report is released after payment is confirmed.

      How do I know if a title deed is genuine?

      A website cannot authenticate a title. Proper verification needs an official search at the land registry, survey evidence on the ground and, where appropriate, legal review by an advocate. We help you gather and read that evidence, and tell you what still needs to be confirmed.

      I live abroad. How can I buy land in Kenya safely?

      Verify before you send money. Check the seller's identity against the title, insist on seeing the title or a certified copy, have a person you trust obtain an official search, and have your own advocate review the agreement. Pay only through an advocate's client account, and have someone visit the plot and confirm the beacons. Our Diaspora Land Check follows this sequence. Pressure to pay quickly is a warning sign.

      What should I check before buying a plot?

      That the title is in the seller's name and matches their ID, that a recent official search shows no caution, charge or court order, and that spouse and family consents are in place. Also check whether Land Control Board consent is needed for agricultural land, that rates and land rent are cleared, that beacons match the map, that there is legal road access, and that nobody occupies the plot.

      Can I list my plot for sale or ask for a plot to buy?

      Yes. Use the Buy & Sell section to list a plot or describe the plot you want. Listings and requests are reviewed by our team before they go live, and we contact you first. We are not a party to any sale and do not guarantee any listing, price or seller, so always carry out your own checks before paying.

      How much does a land survey cost?

      Pricing depends on the service, plot size, location, terrain and scope. The price list on this site gives starting figures for selected services. For a quote that fits your plot, send us the county, approximate size and service you need through the callback or WhatsApp option.

      Do you work outside Nairobi?

      Yes. We work across Kenya, with active hubs in Kirinyaga, Embu, Kiambu, Murang'a, Nyeri and Nairobi. For other counties we confirm availability and scope before we commit, so you know the approach and cost up front.

      LEGAL • DATA PROTECTION

      Privacy Policy

      Last updated: 21 October 2026

      Benchmark Land Surveying (“we”, “us”) collects and uses personal data only to deliver the three services on this website: surveying on the ground, land checks for buyers abroad, and buying and selling plots. We handle personal data in line with the Data Protection Act, 2019 of Kenya.

      1. Who is responsible

      Benchmark Land Surveying is responsible for the personal data described here. Contact us at benchmarklandsurveying.ke@gmail.com for any privacy matter.

      2. What we collect, by service

      01 · ON THE GROUND

      Local Ground Survey and professional services. Your name, mobile number, county and plot location, plot size, the service you want, and any note you add. If you share documents such as a title, deed plan or ID copy, we receive those too. Fieldwork produces measurements and coordinates of your parcel.

      02 · BUYING FROM ABROAD

      Diaspora Land Check, Virtual Check and Land Intelligence Check. Your answers to the check, the county and area, your mobile number, whether you live outside Kenya, any documents you upload, and the preliminary result and report we generate from them.

      03 · BUY & SELL

      Buy and Sell Plots. For a listing: title, county, area, size, price, plot type, document type, a note, photos, and the seller’s name and mobile number. For a plot you want to buy: county, area, size, budget, purpose, a note, and your name and mobile number.

      Across the website. “Tell us your story” (county, mobile number and any story you write), callback requests, and client feedback (name, role, county, message and a private mobile number).

      3. How we use it

      • To call or message you about your request, prepare quotations and carry out the service you asked for.
      • To produce preliminary reports and tell you the next professional step.
      • To review listings and feedback before anything is published.
      • To prevent spam and misuse, for example by limiting repeated submissions from one number.
      • To meet legal and professional record-keeping duties, and to improve the service.

      4. Our lawful bases

      We rely on your consent (for example when you tick a box or submit a form), the steps needed to provide a service you requested, our legitimate interest in running a safe and accurate service, and legal obligations. You may withdraw consent at any time without affecting past lawful use.

      5. What is published

      Only two things are ever shown publicly, and only after review: approved client feedback (name, role, county and message) and approved plot listings or plot requests (details and photos, never phone numbers). Your mobile number is kept private. You can ask us to remove anything published about you.

      6. Who we share data with

      • Service providers. We use Google services (forms and scripts, spreadsheets, email and file storage) to receive, store and send your requests, and our own website and assessment tools to generate reports.
      • Contact channels. If you choose to contact us by phone, WhatsApp or email, those services handle your messages under their own policies.
      • Professionals and authorities. Only when your matter needs it and you have instructed us, for example a registry submission or a referral to an advocate or valuer.
      • We do not sell personal data.

      7. Transfers outside Kenya

      Our providers, and clients abroad, mean data may be processed outside Kenya. We take reasonable steps so that it stays protected, as the Data Protection Act requires.

      8. Security and retention

      Access to submissions is limited to Benchmark Land Surveying, approval links are signed so they cannot be forged, and phone numbers are never published. We keep personal data only as long as needed for the purpose it was collected, or as the law and professional records require, and then delete or anonymise it.

      9. Your rights

      You may ask to be informed about, access, correct or delete your personal data, to object to or restrict its use, and to receive a copy in a usable format. Email benchmarklandsurveying.ke@gmail.com from the contact details you gave us. We may need to confirm who you are first, and we will respond within the time the law allows.

      10. Complaints

      Please contact us first so we can put things right. You also have the right to complain to the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner of Kenya.

      11. Browser storage, maps and children

      The website uses browser storage to remember display settings and your latest check reference. Embedded Google Maps may set their own cookies. We do not run advertising trackers. Our services are for adults, and we do not knowingly collect data from children.

      12. Changes

      We will update this page when our services or the law change, and show the date at the top.

      This Policy is a plain-language summary prepared with reference to the Data Protection Act, 2019 and its regulations. It is not legal advice.

      LEGAL • PROFESSIONAL BOUNDARIES

      Disclaimer

      Last updated: 21 October 2026

      Our online tools give you a structured, preliminary view of your land matter. They support your decision. They do not replace a survey, an official search or professional advice.

      1. What a check can and cannot tell you

      A check shows what your information and documents support, what is missing, and what to verify next. The evidence-readiness score measures how complete your evidence is. It is not a legal opinion, a valuation or a guarantee about a parcel.

      2. What it does not do

      • It does not confirm ownership, or issue or validate a title.
      • It does not replace a search at the land registry or other official records.
      • It does not give legal advice, a valuation or a survey result.
      • It cannot detect what you have not told us, or what documents do not show.

      3. Who completes the step

      Where the law requires it, a licensed surveyor, advocate, planner, valuer or the relevant government authority must complete the step. We carry out surveying and mapping work and point you to the right professional for the rest. Using the tools alone does not create a professional-client relationship.

      4. Artificial intelligence

      Parts of the analysis are automated or AI-assisted. Automated output can be incomplete, outdated or wrong, and may not reflect recent changes in law, county rules or records. Please verify it before you rely on it.

      5. Plots and listings

      Community listings are unverified. Even a Benchmark Verified listing reflects only the records reviewed at that time. Carry out your own due diligence and do not pay for land until a qualified professional has confirmed the key records.

      6. County and general information

      County notes and guides are general information and may change. Check current requirements with the relevant office.

      7. Questions

      Email benchmarklandsurveying.ke@gmail.com.
